sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: At various points in our lives, all of us turn to coaches and trainers.
sentences.zh: 在我们人生的不同阶段，我们所有人都会向教练和导师求助。

sentences.en: If you're a student-athlete, you might need a coach to improve your tennis stroke or soccer footwork.
sentences.zh: 如果你是一名学生运动员，你可能需要一位教练来改进你的网球击球动作或足球脚法。

sentences.en: If you need to take up a musical instrument in your 30s, you'll need the help of a piano teacher or guitar instructor.
sentences.zh: 如果你在30多岁时想学习一门乐器，你需要钢琴老师或吉他导师的帮助。

sentences.en: If you decide you want to learn a new language in your 50s, you sign up for classes with an expert in that language.
sentences.zh: 如果你决定在50多岁时学习一门新语言，你会报名参加精通该语言的专家的课程。

sentences.en: But there are lots of domains in our lives where many of us never dream of recruiting the help of a coach.
sentences.zh: 但我们生活中有许多领域，许多人从未想过要请教练来帮忙。

sentences.en: That's because we feel we are masters in those domains already.
sentences.zh: 那是因为我们觉得自己已经是那些领域的行家里手了。

sentences.en: We don't need a coach to help us breathe or walk or talk.
sentences.zh: 我们不需要教练来教我们如何呼吸、走路或说话。

sentences.en: Or do we?
sentences.zh: 真的是这样吗？

sentences.en: Just because we've done something a long time doesn't mean we are doing it right.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为我们某件事做了很久，并不意味着我们做得对。

sentences.en: Just because we feel we are skilled at something doesn't mean we don't have plenty of room for improvement.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为我们觉得自己擅长某事，并不意味着我们没有很大的改进空间。

sentences.en: Today on the show, we focus on a skill that seems so commonplace that many of us fail to see how difficult it is to do well.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目中，我们关注一种技能，它看起来如此寻常，以至于我们许多人都没有意识到把它做好有多么困难。

sentences.en: We're going to look at how we engage in conversation and the things we can do to get better at it.
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨我们是如何进行对话的，以及我们可以做些什么来把它做得更好。

sentences.en: Learning to talk.
sentences.zh: 学会说话。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 本周《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: When discussing the children in our lives, we say they learn to talk at age one or two.
sentences.zh: 当讨论我们生活中的孩子时，我们会说他们在岁或两岁时学会说话。

sentences.en: For the late bloomers, maybe it's three or four.
sentences.zh: 对于那些大器晚成的人来说，也许是三岁或四岁。

sentences.en: We make it sound as if learning to talk is something we master early and then practice without a problem as adults.
sentences.zh: 我们把学会说话说得好像是我们很早就掌握了，然后成年后就能毫无问题地进行实践的一样。

sentences.en: But it turns out that most of us have a lot to learn when it comes to having conversations that are dynamic, engaging, and meaningful.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，谈到如何进行充满活力、引人入胜且有意义的对话时，我们大多数人还有很多东西要学。

sentences.en: Alison Woodbrooks is a behavioral scientist at Harvard Business School.
sentences.zh: 艾莉森·伍德布鲁克斯是哈佛商学院的行为科学家。

sentences.en: For many years now, she has studied the science of conversation.
sentences.zh: 多年来，她一直致力于研究对话科学。

sentences.en: Alison Woodbrooks, welcome to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 艾莉森·伍德布鲁克斯，欢迎来到《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.zh: 孩子们拿着巨大的巧克力棒时，我开始和其中一个邻居搭话，

sentences.en: one of these family members that I had didn't know before.
sentences.zh: 也就是我之前不认识的其中一位家庭成员。

sentences.en: And it was a man from Ohio.
sentences.zh: 那是一个来自俄亥俄州的男人。

sentences.en: I overheard him saying that he was from Ohio.
sentences.zh: 我无意中听到他说他是俄亥俄州人。

sentences.en: And so as the two of us became isolated, I quickly started asking questions about Ohio.
sentences.zh: 于是，当只剩下我们俩时，我赶紧开始问有关俄亥俄州的问题。

sentences.en: Where are you from in Ohio?
sentences.zh: 你在俄亥俄州哪儿长大？

sentences.en: Did you go to Ohio State?
sentences.zh: 你上过俄亥俄州立大学吗？

sentences.en: Oh, I've been to German Village.
sentences.zh: 哦，我去过德国村。

sentences.en: It's such a quaint part of Columbus.
sentences.zh: 那是哥伦布一个很有古韵的地方。

sentences.en: So I'm using all of my Ohio knowledge to kind of find a way into this conversation.
sentences.zh: 所以我把我所有的俄亥俄州知识都用上了，想方设法切入这个话题。

sentences.en: I talk, my husband's from Michigan, so I start talking about Big Ten football or,
sentences.zh: 我聊起我丈夫是密歇根州人，于是我开始聊十大联盟橄榄球，或者

sentences.en: you know, the rivalry between Ohio State and Michigan, and I'm really going for it.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，俄亥俄州立大学和密歇根大学之间的宿敌对决，我真的豁出去了。

sentences.en: But really, no matter what I say about Ohio, it doesn't seem like we can find a way out of it.
sentences.zh: 但说实话，不管我怎么聊俄亥俄州，我们好像都找不到一个自然的突破口。

sentences.en: We're sort of stuck.
sentences.zh: 我们有点卡住了。

sentences.en: We're stuck in Ohio.
sentences.zh: 我们陷在俄亥俄州了。

sentences.en: You're trapped in Ohio.
sentences.zh: 你被困在俄亥俄州了。

sentences.en: We're trapped in Ohio.
sentences.zh: 我们被困在俄亥俄州了。

sentences.en: He's not really giving me a lot in response to my questions.
sentences.zh: 对于我的问题，他并没有给我太多的回应。

sentences.en: And I chalked it up to a sort of small talk failure.
sentences.zh: 我把这归咎于一次失败的闲聊。

sentences.en: And I said, you know what?
sentences.zh: 我说，你知道吗？

sentences.en: I think I'm going to try again with this guy later in the night.
sentences.zh: 我想今晚晚些时候再跟这家伙聊聊。

sentences.en: So in some ways, what I'm hearing, Alison, is that this guy might have been a milder version of the blind date you went on,
sentences.zh: 艾莉森，从某种程度上听起来，这个家伙可能就是你多年前经历的那场相亲的

sentences.en: you know, many years earlier.
sentences.zh: 温和版。

sentences.en: He also was not very curious about what was going on in your life.
sentences.zh: 他同样对你生活里发生的事不怎么好奇。

sentences.en: He also was someone who was not asking you many questions.
sentences.zh: 他也属于那种不怎么问你问题的人。

sentences.en: I understand that the value that you place on question asking stems from a backstory involving your mom.
sentences.zh: 我了解到，你对提问的重视源于一个关于你妈妈的背景故事。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: My mom is an amazing sort of intuitive psychologiSt.
sentences.zh: 我妈妈是个了不起的、直觉敏锐的心理学家。

sentences.en: And when I was young, probably starting in late middle school, but definitely high school, we would drive home from social engagements.
sentences.zh: 当我年轻的时候，大概从初中晚期开始，但绝对是在高中时，我们经常从社交聚会的车上回家。

sentences.en: And she would often ask us, hey, did you talk to anybody who was a really good question asker?
sentences.zh: 她经常问我们，嘿，你们有没有跟一个特别会提问的人聊天？

sentences.en: And I'm grateful to my mom for that.
sentences.zh: 我很感激我妈妈这一点。

sentences.en: It made me sort of pique my interest in interpersonal dynamics.
sentences.zh: 这让我对人际互动产生了浓厚的兴趣。

sentences.en: You've gotten to know a professional matchmaker named Rachel Greenwald, and she has a great term for people who lack conversational curiosity.
sentences.zh: 你认识了一位名叫雷切尔·格林沃尔德的专业红娘，她对那些缺乏聊天好奇心的人有一个很好的称呼。

sentences.en: Tell me about her, Alison.
sentences.zh: 跟我讲讲她吧，艾莉森。

sentences.en: Yes, Rachel Greenwald.
sentences.zh: 对，雷切尔·格林沃尔德。

sentences.en: I think she's amazing.
sentences.zh: 我觉得她太棒了。

sentences.en: She's sort of the grand poobah of professional matchmakers.
sentences.zh: 她可以说是专业红娘里的大咖。

sentences.en: She started out her career as a matchmaker, and then she had so much success that she started training other matchmakers to do this job.
sentences.zh: 她职业生涯刚开始时是一名红娘，后来获得了巨大成功，于是开始培训其他红娘来干这行。

sentences.en: And she said to me, we have a phrase for people who don't ask questions.
sentences.zh: 她对我说，我们对那些不爱提问的人有一个短语。

sentences.en: When you think of people who ask zero questions, especially on a date, we call them ZQs, zero questioners.
sentences.zh: 当你想到那些完全不提问的人，尤其是在约会时，我们称他们为ZQ，也就是零提问者（Zero Questioners）。

sentences.en: And there's this quote, she says, you know, they say curiosity killed the cat, but on a date, curiosity does not kill the date.
sentences.zh: 有这么一句名言，她说，你知道的，人们说好奇害死猫，但在约会上，好奇不会害死约会。

sentences.en: In fact, the ZQ kills the date.
sentences.zh: 事实上，ZQ（零提问者）才会害死约会。

sentences.en: So you have IQ, you have EQ, and now you have ZQ.
sentences.zh: 所以你有智商（IQ）、情商（EQ），现在你还有了ZQ。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So there's a more insidious form of the same problem.
sentences.zh: 所以还有一种更潜移默化的同类问题。

sentences.en: And here the person does ask questions, but the questions do not stem from curiosity about the other person.
sentences.zh: 这种情况下，这个人确实会问问题，但这些问题并不是出于对对方的好奇。

sentences.en: You call this boomerasking.
sentences.zh: 你把这叫做回旋镖式提问（Boomerasking）。

sentences.en: What is boomerasking, Alison?
sentences.zh: 什么是回旋镖式提问，艾莉森？

sentences.en: Boomerasking is not people over 50 who ask questions.
sentences.zh: 回旋镖式提问不是指50岁以上的人提问题。

sentences.en: It is, it is, it's, it's, it's named after the arc of a boomerang.
sentences.zh: 它是，它是，它是，它是根据回旋镖的轨迹命名的。

sentences.en: And so imagine you're throwing a boomerang and the boomerang has this arc that goes out and then comes around and comes right back to you.
sentences.zh: 所以想象一下你扔出一个回旋镖，回旋镖划过一个弧线飞出去，然后转个弯直接飞回你手里。

sentences.en: And the structure of boomerasking is, you ask a question to your partner, you let them answer the question, but then you bring the focus of the conversation right back to yourself.
sentences.zh: 回旋镖式提问的结构是：你向伴侣提问，让他们回答问题，但随后你立刻把谈话的焦点转回到你自己身上。

sentences.en: So it would be as if I said to you, Shankar, how was your weekend?
sentences.zh: 这就好比如果我对你（尚卡尔）说，你周末过得怎么样？

sentences.en: And I say, oh, the weekend was fun.
sentences.zh: 然后我说，哦，这个周末真好玩。

sentences.en: You know, we went to a nice restaurant and went for a walk in the park.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我们去了一家不错的餐厅，还在公园里散了步。

sentences.en: Oh, well, I actually went skydiving with Harry Styles and it was terrific.
sentences.zh: 哦，其实我和哈里·斯泰尔斯一起去跳伞了，棒极了。

sentences.en: So you let your partner answer, but then you almost ignore what they share with you and you bring the focus right back to yourself.
sentences.zh: 所以你让伴侣回答，但接着你几乎无视了他们分享的内容，直接把焦点拉回你自己身上。

sentences.en: It makes your partner feel like you weren't interested in their answer in the first place.
sentences.zh: 这会让你的伴侣觉得你一开始就对他们的回答不感兴趣。

sentences.en: You were just asking as a way to set up your own disclosure.
sentences.zh: 你提问只是为了引出你自己的倾诉。

sentences.en: It's a sort of thinly veiled way to hide your own selfishness, your own egocentrism.
sentences.zh: 这是一种掩盖你自私和自我中心、欲盖弥彰的方式。

sentences.en: There's another trapdoor in conversations that might be familiar to many people.
sentences.zh: 对话中还有另一个许多人可能都很熟悉的陷阱。

sentences.en: I want to play you a clip from the 1993 movie Wayne's World 2, where Wayne and Garth are being interviewed by a radio host about a big concert they are excited about.
sentences.zh: 我想放一段1993年电影《反斗智多星2》（Wayne's World 2）的片段，其中韦恩和加思正在接受一位电台主持人的采访，谈论他们非常期待的一场大型音乐会。

sentences.en: All right, our special guests right now, Wayne Campbell, Garth Elgar, Wayne's World, Wayne's World.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们现在的特邀嘉宾是韦恩·坎贝尔、加思·埃尔加，韦恩的世界，韦恩的世界。

sentences.en: All right, talking about Wayne's Stock, very exciting, big event.
sentences.zh: 好的，来聊聊韦恩音乐节，非常令人兴奋的大型活动。

sentences.en: Everybody's excited, huh?
sentences.zh: 大家都挺激动的吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's going to be a big concert at Adelaide Stevenson Park.
sentences.zh: 对，这将是阿德莱德·史蒂文森公园的一场盛大音乐会。

sentences.en: It's just going to be a big party, you know, we've got some great bands coming, like Aerosmith.
sentences.zh: 这会是一场盛大的派对，你知道的，我们会请来一些很棒的乐队，比如史密斯飞船（Aerosmith）。

sentences.en: I just want to remind everybody that there's still plenty of tickets left, but that's no reason to wait till the last minute.
sentences.zh: 我只想提醒大家，还有很多票剩下，但这可不是拖到最后一分钟才买的理由。

sentences.en: Because it's just a chance for the city of Aurora to do something fun and to put the city on the map.
sentences.zh: 因为这只是奥罗拉市做一件有趣的事并让这座城市名扬天下的机会。

sentences.en: It's a lot of work.
sentences.zh: 这工作量可不小。

sentences.en: Oh, well, work is hard.
sentences.zh: 哦，工作本来就很难。

sentences.en: You're not really listening to me, are you?
sentences.zh: 你根本没有在听我说话，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, I could say anything right now, like you're a complete tool.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我现在说什么都行，比如你是个彻头彻尾的笨蛋。

sentences.en: But you wouldn't hear it.
sentences.zh: 但你根本听不进去。

sentences.en: So, Alison, how often is it that people in conversation fail to listen to one another?
sentences.zh: 所以，艾莉森，人们在对话中听不进去对方说话的情况有多普遍？

sentences.en: Oh, Shakur, this happens all the time.
sentences.zh: 哦，尚卡尔，这经常发生。

sentences.en: I think the reason this clip is so funny to us is because it's so relatable.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这个片段之所以让我们觉得这么搞笑，是因为它太真实了。

sentences.en: We have done research recently to show that people's minds are wandering 24% of the time during conversation.
sentences.zh: 我们最近做过研究表明，在对话过程中，人们的思想有24%的时间都在开小差。

sentences.en: And this was based on their own self-reports.
sentences.zh: 这是根据他们自己的自我报告得出的。

sentences.en: So we interrupted them every five minutes in a conversation and asked them, were you listening attentively to your partner or was your mind wandering?
sentences.zh: 所以我们在对话中每五分钟打断他们一次，问他们：你是在专心听伴侣说话，还是在走神？

sentences.en: And 24% of the time they say, actually, my mind was wandering.
sentences.zh: 24%的时间里他们都说，其实，我的思想在开小差。

sentences.en: I wasn't listening to my partner.
sentences.zh: 我根本没在听伴侣说话。

sentences.en: We suspect this is an underestimate because people know that it's sort of embarrassing to not be listening to their partner.
sentences.zh: 我们怀疑这是一个被严重低估的数据，因为人们知道没听伴侣说话是件挺尴尬的事。

sentences.en: You see this happen during video calls or like on Zoom.
sentences.zh: 你会发现这种现象在视频通话或Zoom上经常发生。

sentences.en: People are smiling and nodding at the camera even while they're like to the side texting their friend or making a grocery list because there are these norms of politeness, right?
sentences.zh: 人们对着镜头微笑点头，哪怕他们同时还在旁边给朋友发短信或是列购物清单，因为存在着这些礼貌规范，对吧？

sentences.en: We know that we should make our partners feel like we're listening to them.
sentences.zh: 我们知道我们应该让伴侣觉得我们在听他们说话。

sentences.en: For most of us, talking doesn't seem hard.
sentences.zh: 对大多数人来说，说话似乎并不难。

sentences.en: We open our mouths and words come out.
sentences.zh: 我们张开嘴，话就出来了。

sentences.en: But as we go through life, it is usually the case that the people around us are not telling us when they find us boring or irritating or just plain offensive.
sentences.zh: 但随着我们经历人生，身边的往往不会直接告诉我们他们觉得我们无聊、烦人或纯粹冒犯了他们。

sentences.en: When we come back, how to make our conversations more engaging.
sentences.zh: 广告回来后，教你如何让谈话变得更引人入胜。

sentences.en: You're listening to Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 您收听的是《隐藏的大脑》（Hidden Brain）。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: I have a vivid memory of a great conversation right before the COVID pandemic struck.
sentences.zh: 我对新冠大流行爆发前的一次绝佳对话有着清晰的记忆。

sentences.en: I was sitting in a New Orleans restaurant with four researchers who were in town to attend a psychology conference.
sentences.zh: 我当时正坐在新奥尔良的一家餐厅里，同座的有四位研究人员，他们是来这里参加心理学会议的。

sentences.en: The conversation felt like a rapid-fire game of ping-pong.
sentences.zh: 那场谈话就像是一场节奏明快的乒乓球赛。

sentences.en: It felt effortless.
sentences.zh: 感觉毫不费力。

sentences.en: It was glorious.
sentences.zh: 真是太棒了。

sentences.en: At Harvard Business School, Alison Woodbrook studies how we can all have many more memorable conversations.
sentences.zh: 在哈佛商学院，艾莉森·伍德布鲁克斯研究了我们如何才能进行更多令人难忘的对话。

sentences.en: She is the author of Talk, The Science of Conversation, and The Art of Being Ourselves.
sentences.zh: 她是《谈话：对话的科学与做自己的艺术》（Talk, The Science of Conversation, and The Art of Being Ourselves）的作者。

sentences.en: Alison, I have a strong belief that authentic conversations must just emerge naturally, and I suspect many listeners have the same belief.
sentences.zh: 艾莉森，我深信真诚的对话必须是自然而然流露的，我猜很多听众也有同感。

sentences.en: You say this is a mistake.
sentences.zh: 你说这是一个误区。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We often talk about this idea of the myth of naturalness.
sentences.zh: 我们经常讨论“自然性神话”这个概念。

sentences.en: So many of my students and so many people believe that good conversationalists are born, that they are extroverted and gregarious and charismatic, and that's just how they are.
sentences.zh: 我的许多学生和许多人都认为，优秀的谈话者是天生的，他们外向、社交、有个人魅力，他们本来就是那样。

sentences.en: It's their personality.
sentences.zh: 这是他们的性格。

sentences.en: But so much of the work that I've done over the last 15 years suggests that many, many things about conversation are very learnable.
sentences.zh: 但我在过去15里所做的大量研究表明，关于对话的很多很多事情其实是非常可以通过后天学习掌握的。

sentences.en: Even for the most introverted, shy, awkward people who really think that they weren't born charismatic, these things can be learned as well.
sentences.zh: 即便是那些最内向、害羞、笨拙，真觉得自己天生没有个人魅力的人，这些技巧也是可以学会的。

sentences.en: And one of the most valuable things that we've learned in our research and in my class is this idea of topic preparation.
sentences.zh: 而在我们的研究和我的课堂上学到的最有价值的事情之一，就是“话题准备”这个概念。

sentences.en: Topic preparation is literally just thinking about what are possible things that we could talk about before the conversation begins.
sentences.zh: 话题准备实际上就是在对话开始之前，思考一下我们可以聊些什么可能的话题。

sentences.en: It's not complex.
sentences.zh: 这并不复杂。

sentences.en: And many people find this idea of preparing for a conversation, especially for people that we're close to outside of work, to be very aversive.
sentences.zh: 很多人觉得为对话做准备——尤其是和工作之外的亲近之人对话——是一件非常令人排斥的事。

sentences.en: You sort of have this instinct that I shouldn't need to prepare for a conversation with someone that I'm close to.
sentences.zh: 你内心有一种本能，觉得我不应该需要为和一个亲近之人的对话做准备。

sentences.en: We'll get together and I'll know exactly what to talk about or we'll have many things to talk about.
sentences.zh: 我们聚在一起，我自然知道该聊什么，或者我们有无数的话题可聊。

sentences.en: And many of my students feel this way, too.
sentences.zh: 我的很多学生也是这么想的。

sentences.en: They're sort of like, why are you making me prepare for a casual conversation?
sentences.zh: 他们有点像在说，你凭什么让我为一次随意的谈话做准备？

sentences.en: And in some ways, we do this to some extent in work settings, right?
sentences.zh: 从某种程度上说，我们在工作环境中多多少少都会这样做，对吧？

sentences.en: So we can have a meeting, for example, and there's an agenda that's circulated before the meeting saying, here's what we're going to talk about.
sentences.zh: 比如我们可以开个会，会前会分发一份议程，上面写着：这就是我们要讨论的内容。

sentences.en: But that seems OK in work settings in ways that it seems difficult to do in personal settings.
sentences.zh: 但在工作环境中觉得没问题的事情，在个人生活中做起来似乎就很难。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's slightly more normative, more common in work settings where it's more common to have an agenda ahead of time or at least somebody has thought about it.
sentences.zh: 对，这在工作环境中更合乎常规、更常见，提前有议程或者至少有人提前想过这些事更普遍。

sentences.en: Although you might be surprised by how rare it is, even in work settings.
sentences.zh: 尽管你可能会惊讶于这种做法即使在工作环境中也多么少见。

sentences.en: I was working with Google a few years ago who had this huge campaign within Google.
sentences.zh: 几年前我和谷歌合作过，他们在谷歌内部发起了一场轰轰烈烈的运动。

sentences.en: And the only goal was to get people to think ahead about their meetings even a little bit.
sentences.zh: 唯一的目的就是让大家哪怕稍微提前对会议做点思考。

sentences.en: Like they had such a problem with people just showing up and not thinking ahead that they started this huge campaign.
sentences.zh: 比如他们对人们开会直接去却不提前思考的现象深恶痛绝，以至于发起了这场声势浩大的运动。

sentences.en: So even at work, I think there is sort of a resistance to topic prep or at least a lack of making time to think ahead about our conversations.
sentences.zh: 所以即使在工作中，我觉得大家也对提前准备话题存在某种排斥，或者至少缺乏花时间提前思考对话的习惯。

sentences.en: And certainly in casual conversations, people feel like they don't need to, and so they don't.
sentences.zh: 当然，在平时的闲聊中，人们觉得没必要，所以也就不去做了。

sentences.en: So you have found that topic preparation can be helpful even when we are talking with someone who is close to us.
